text:
maya (Product): quick sync — ACME requested we accelerate the Adaptive Rerank rollout. They want a faster ramp; ops wants safe guards. need a decision on prioritization framework + exact canary sequencing. proposing RICE-based prioritization then a conservative rollout. thoughts? :thinking_face:

alex (Eng): RICE is useful but it flattens sequencing tradeoffs. If reach is huge we might still want slower canaries because of cost and GPU churn. what's the hard requirement from ACME on timeline?

nora (PM): ACME says they need it in ~3 weeks to hit their QBR. High business impact for them, medium confidence (new dataset). They've offered a pilot seat (negotiation). If we score with RICE: reach=6, impact=8, confidence=5, effort=4 -> score 60. That pushes it up but not top-urgent.

sophia (Data): from experiment/statistics side: to detect a 5% lift in rerank CTR with 80% power we need ~18k impressions per variant. If we do 1% canary that takes too long. Either increase canary % or run shadow mode + offline eval to bootstrap.

liam (SRE): we need clear stop/rollback criteria. I'd suggest: error rate > 1.5x baseline OR p95 latency +50ms OR negative quality signal from eval job for 2 consecutive windows. Also need a runbook for auto-traffic-fallback to stable model (route -> stable endpoint).

zach (EngOps): capacity note: burst to 25% for canary window will require warm GPUs. If we schedule during low-traffic window we can reuse capacity, but committing to 25% for 4h ties up nodes. Ops prefers staged: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with watch windows.

maya (Product): proposed rollout plan (v1):
```
1) shadow run (2 days) + offline eval on ACME dataset
2) canary: 5% for 3h -> evaluate metrics (ctr, latency, errors, quality_eval)
3) if green: 20% for 6h -> 50% for 24h -> 100%
stop criteria: any stop -> immediate rollback and notify ACME + internal oncall
```
Comments: shadow phase helps address Sophia's sample-size issue while keeping production risk low.

alex (Eng): shadow + small canary is good. But curious about rollback granularity: do we flip traffic only at edge-router or do we use in-service weighted routing? edge-router flip is faster but coarser. weighted routing requires more infra work. Recommend edge flip with pre-built routing keys.

liam (SRE): edge flip + pre-created stable hook is simplest for quick rollback. Make sure canary-bot alert threshold ties into SLO channels and triggers a runbook step. Also confirm metrics aggregation window (we prefer 5m for infra, 30m for quality signals).

sophia (Data): To address power: do shadow + launch analysis with Bayesian sequential testing so we can escalate earlier if posterior crosses threshold. That reduces required sample size vs fixed-horizon A/B. Need analytics owner and pre-registered metrics.

nora (PM): on prioritization framework — suggestion: use a hybrid: apply RICE to decide whether to accept request into the sprint pipeline, then use impact-vs-effort + risk-adjusted sequencing to pick rollout cadence. Rationale: RICE for triage, sequencing needs safety-first heuristics.

alex (Eng): agreed. Practically: if RICE score >50 and ACME SLA is high, we slot it. But sequencing decision should consider SRE/EngOps constraints + Sophia's sampling plan.

maya (Product): decision check: adopt hybrid approach. For this request we accept (RICE ~60). Rollout plan = shadow 48h -> 5% 3h -> 20% 6h -> 50% 24h -> 100%. Stop criteria as Liam listed. Data will run sequential test and report bayes posterior every window. Ops will provision warm nodes for 20% jump. Eng to prepare edge flip/rollback hook.

alex (Eng): I'll own edge routing changes and rollback hook. ETA: 4 days to implement + test in staging. Need EngOps to reserve capacity windows.

zach (EngOps): reserving a warm pool for 6/12/24h windows — can do. booking in infra calendar now. Also will add a preflight checklist (certs, KMS access, model artifact pin).

sophia (Data): I'll draft the analysis plan with priors and stopping thresholds. Will share pre-registration doc by EOD tomorrow.

liam (SRE): I'll add the alerting rules to the oncall runbook and wire canary-bot to the channel for automated green/red posts.

maya (Product): great. final ask: product to create rollout ticket with RICE summary + link to ACME pilot agreement and attach the runbook + pre-registration doc before kickoff. I'll queue it for PM review. :white_check_mark:

canary-bot: ✅ Canary pipeline scheduled: shadow -> canary. Will post automated progress updates to #product during rollout.

alex (Eng): one more tradeoff note: quicker ramp reduces time-to-value for ACME but increases cost and operational risk. we documented the choice above. If legal/compliance needs extra review, flag now.

nora (PM): flag: ACME asked for a SOC2 data flow review. product will coordinate with security; might add 2 business days. That could push timeline from 3 weeks to 3.5 weeks.

maya (Product): ok capturing that. action items: (1) Maya: ticket + RICE + ACME doc, (2) Alex: edge routing + rollback hook, (3) Sophia: pre-reg analytics, (4) Zach: capacity reservation, (5) Liam: alerts & runbook. Revisit in 48h for go/no-go.

alex (Eng): :thumbsup:

sophia (Data): :eyes:

liam (SRE): noted, will add escalation paging policy.

zach (EngOps): booked infra slots and left comment in ticket about cost impact.

maya (Product): thanks team — closing thread for now, will reopen with kickoff info.
